audits.text:
## generic_resize_gen3

**Reproduced lesson-identifiability defect.** Audited generator SHA-256: `f679aeaa2125e764964bd870999b3418a26b2bf4cacceeb72345cb974a70d189`. No target files were changed.

The deterministic search in `checks/audit/generic_resize_gen3/search_ambiguity.py` examined 43,104 easy seeds (`0..43103`) and found a concrete ambiguous lesson at seed `43103`. Its intended scale map has row repeats `[2,2,2]` and column repeats `[1,1,2,1]`. The rival uses the same row repeats and columns `[1,1,1,2]`. In every one of the three demonstrations, source columns 2 and 3 are identical, so both programs produce the stored output. The held-out input separates those columns; the two programs then give different answers (the first difference is at zero-based output row 2, column 3).

`checks/audit/generic_resize_gen3/ambiguity.json` retains the full lesson, authoritative output, rival output, source hash, seed, and replay command. `checks/audit/generic_resize_gen3/verify_racket.py` independently replays both programs through the Racket bridge; `checks/audit/generic_resize_gen3/racket-parity.json` records that the intended program matches all four stored outputs, the alternate matches all 3/3 demonstrations, and the alternate differs on the 1/1 query. This is a teaching defect, not a label-parity defect, and the generated input belongs to the target’s ordinary easy-seed domain.

The same search found a simpler family overlap at seed `23`: row repeats `[1,1,1]`, column repeats `[2,2,2]`, which is ordinary horizontal doubling despite the generator’s “gen3” parameterization. A repair should resample until demonstrations distinguish every adjacent row/column boundary whose repeat count can alter the query, or add an executable lesson-identifiability gate over local scale-map rivals. Constant-per-axis tasks may also merit rejection when this generator is intended to teach non-uniform scaling.

audits.text:
## generic_resize_gen3

**Reproduced lesson-identifiability defect; audited source unchanged.** Generator
SHA-256: `f679aeaa2125e764964bd870999b3418a26b2bf4cacceeb72345cb974a70d189`.
A prior unresolved audit supplied seed `43103` as a lead; I copied its full
source-bound lesson into `checks/audit/generic_resize_gen3/ambiguity.json` and
independently replayed both programs against the current packet source through
the protected Racket bridge.

The intended scale map uses row repeats `[2,2,2]` and column repeats
`[1,1,2,1]`. A rival with the same row repeats and columns `[1,1,1,2]` matches
all **3/3 demonstrations** because source columns 2 and 3 happen to be identical
in every demonstration, but it disagrees on the **1/1 query**, where those
columns differ. `checks/audit/generic_resize_gen3/racket-parity.json` records
`all_intended_match=true`, `alternate_fits_all_train=true`, and
`alternate_differs_on_test=true`; the replay command and console are retained
beside it. This is a generated teaching defect, not a label-parity defect.

A repair should reject or resample a task until the demonstrations distinguish
neighboring row/column repeat assignments that can change a query, ideally via
an executable scale-map rival gate. No files under the audited generator were
modified.
